summary.headline: SAMIL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR38,280 crore, EBITDA up 23% to INR3,353 crore, margin 8.8% (down ~20 bps YoY on acquisitions).
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly and half-yearly revenue, with growth driven by the Autoelectric and Yutaka Giken acquisitions and a strong wiring harness business. Normalized PAT rose 37% YoY to INR1,175 crore, and the booked order book reached a record USD 106 billion. Margins were pressured by acquisition integration and commodity inflation (copper, aluminium, polymers), partly offset by cost optimisation and pass-throughs; management said margins excluding acquisitions improved both YoY and QoQ. Net debt rose to INR11,292 crore on working capital (copper), capex and leases, with leverage stable at 0.8x.

financial_highlights.change: Stable QoQ; policy ceiling 2.5x, internal aspiration below 1.5x

segments.name: Wiring harness
segments.commentary: Grew about 68% in Q2; roughly one-third of growth attributed to Autoelectric acquisition, balance to North American commercial vehicles (+40%+) and India. Autoelectric consolidated for full quarter; serves German OEMs (BMW largest customer, plus Daimler, Porsche, Audi) and adds passenger-car harness capability outside India.

segments.name: Emerging businesses
segments.commentary: Quarterly EBITDA of INR543 crore, which management said exceeded vision systems and integrated assemblies. Aerospace grew more than 20% YoY; Rotary Connectors acquisition announced. Yutaka Giken consolidated for two months; combined Autoelectric and Yutaka expected to deliver around USD 2 billion annual revenue in first full year, with margins slightly below group level.

segments.name: Consumer electronics
segments.commentary: Greenfield plants 1 and 2 operating; GF3 (largest plant) in trial production with commercial production targeted for Q4 FY27. Total capex for the business about INR7,500 crore, up from an initial INR2,600 crore, attributed to higher capacity and backward integration.

segments.name: Modules and polymer (MPP)
segments.commentary: Management cited growth in India and premium customers, offset by European weakness tied to EV platform decisions; cost reduction and footprint reorganisation ongoing. No quantified segment figures given in the call.

segments.name: Medical and health
segments.commentary: First plant operational in Chennai; order book growing organically; acquired Irillic (diagnostics devices), which is ramping up. Management described the segment as slower to scale post-COVID.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 capex guided at INR6,000 crore (plus or minus 10%); about 60% earmarked for non-automotive businesses.
17 facilities in various stages of development; 10 expected to become operational in FY27.
Consumer electronics GF3 commercial production in Q4 FY27; management expects visible progress within about two quarters and full capacity by next year.
Management does not guide on margins; pass-through of commodity costs has about a 3-month lag (sometimes 6).
Commercial vehicle production expected to keep positive momentum in H2 FY27; Europe contracting.
Automation: over 1,000 projects targeted by next year, with about 940 already in pipeline.
Investor Day scheduled for the 2.5-year mark of the five-year (Vision 2030) plan.
capex_capacity: Q2 capex INR1,971 crore; H1 capex INR3,585 crore, in line with FY27 guidance of INR6,000 crore.
PCB greenfield facility operational in the quarter, providing backward integration for lighting and vision systems.
Five additional facility expansions announced in Q2; total 17 at various stages, 10 to go live in FY27; all in emerging markets.
GF3 consumer electronics plant (largest) nearly complete, running pilots; total consumer electronics capex about INR7,500 crore.
Rotary Connectors acquisition announced to broaden aerospace and defence capability.
demand_pricing: Global light vehicle production down 2.3% YoY in H1 FY27: China -5.5%, North America -3.8%, Europe -0.6%, India +15%.
Global commercial vehicle production up 7.6%; North America +43.6%, India +18.9%.
Order book at a record USD 106 billion (USD 96 billion in FY26; USD 59 billion in FY23); about 13% CAGR FY23 to H1 FY27.
Input cost pressure from copper, aluminium and polymers; copper price rise increased working capital; pass-through negotiated customer by customer.
Management said the US has won many contracts that should ramp over the next couple of years; Europe in transition as OEMs reset product lines.

qa_highlights.question: Rishabh Rathi (Goldman Sachs): Are cost pass-throughs done, and what margin outlook for modules/polymers and wiring harness in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not guide margins; some pass-throughs resolved, others pending, and volatility makes these negotiations continuous. Cost actions include headcount reduction, AI and automation.

qa_highlights.question: Jyoti Singh (Haitong): How much of wiring harness growth came from Autoelectric, and is the trajectory sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: About one-third of the roughly 68% growth came from the acquisition; the rest from North American CV strength and India. Management declined to forecast beyond following customer directives but is capacity-ready.

qa_highlights.question: Amyn Pirani (J.P. Morgan): Consolidation timing of Yutaka Giken and expected consumer electronics backward-integration margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Yutaka consolidated for two months, Autoelectric for three. Management would not give a margin target, saying the business is in year one and that it targets 40% ROCE over a five-year plan; it expects the business to be accretive.

qa_highlights.question: Raghunandhan (Nuvama): Can aerospace reach USD 1 billion revenue before Vision 2030, and organically?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said USD 1 billion would be too low a target; growth needs greenfields and some inorganic additions, with acquisition opportunities live but undisclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Kumar Rakesh (BNP Paribas): Why has consumer electronics capex risen from about INR2,600 crore to INR7,500 crore, and when is full ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase reflects higher capacity plus backward integration into more processes and products. Full capacity expected by next year, about two quarters after kick-off.

qa_highlights.question: Manpreet Arora (Northern Lights): Will the company acquire capabilities proactively in aerospace and emerging businesses, and how is Yutaka being integrated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said acquisitions are customer-led, with customers often asking the company to take over distressed suppliers. Yutaka already supplies Indian OEMs and two-wheeler brake discs and exhaust, with ASEAN and global footprint.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from acquisition integration (Autoelectric, Yutaka) and commodity inflation; pass-through lag of about 3 months.
Net debt rise to INR11,292 crore; working capital intensity from copper prices.
Europe volume contraction and OEM product-line resets; Chinese competition in Europe.
GF3 consumer electronics ramp timing (commercial production targeted Q4 FY27) and logistics challenges.
Regulatory timing uncertainty for India ADAS/AIS-184 driver monitoring requirements that may affect vision systems demand.
Company asked for more granular quarterly disclosure of emerging business segments.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order book and diversification, but cautious on margins and near-term Europe demand; management repeatedly declined to give margin or volume guidance, citing volatility.
key_quotes: Our booked business has reached USD 106 billion and providing strong growth and reflecting the confidence our customers place on Motherson across businesses and geographies.

Excluding the impact of acquisitions, margins improved both year-on-year and sequentially, supported by ongoing engagement with customers to secure input cost pass-throughs, along with benefits of our operating leverage.
We stick to the 40% ROCEs, and of course, we are only going to go after businesses where we can see a sight to be able to get those.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 capex at INR6,000 crore (±10%), held with H1 at INR3,585 crore, and does not give a revenue number; growth is backed by a record USD 106 billion order book, GF3 consumer electronics plant targeted for Q4 FY27 and 10 of 17 facilities going live in FY27, with Autoelectric and Yutaka acquisitions adding inorganic growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 8.8% (about -20 bps YoY) on acquisition integration and copper/aluminium/polymer inflation; management does not guide margins, says ex-acquisition margins improved YoY and QoQ, and pass-through lag is about 3 months (sometimes 6).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 10 of 17 facilities go live in FY27 and GF3 consumer electronics plant (largest) targets commercial production in Q4 FY27 after trial runs; PCB and medical plant already commissioned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Record USD 106 billion booked order book (USD 96 billion in FY26) and H1 revenue up 22% YoY, with North American CV volumes up 43.6% and US contracts ramping over the next couple of years; offset by global LV production down 2.3% and Europe contracting.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex run-rate is firmly held at INR6,000 crore for FY27 (H1 at INR3,585 crore), 17 facilities in development and Rotary Connectors and Irillic deals show continued deployment, and an Investor Day is set for the 2.5-year mark of Vision 2030, so a further capex/expansion announcement is probable.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management does not guide margins or volumes and cites volatility; no raise to the FY27 capex or revenue framework was signalled, and Europe demand is contracting.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Net debt rose to INR11,292 crore from INR9,757 crore and copper-driven working capital is elevated; Europe volumes are falling (global LV production -2.3%, Europe -0.6%) and GF3 ramp depends on logistics, so a slip is possible although leverage is stable at 0.8x.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: GF3 consumer electronics plant (capex about INR7,500 crore, up from INR2,600 crore) targets commercial production in Q4 FY27, with full capacity expected about two quarters later; Irillic diagnostics ramping and aerospace/Rotary Connectors broadening the portfolio.

rows.label: Record USD 106 billion order book converting into US CV/harness ramp
rows.why: Order book at USD 106 billion (USD 96 billion in FY26) with US contracts won that management says should ramp over the next couple of years, and North American CV production up 43.6% in H1 FY27.

rows.label: Emerging-market facility expansions (17 facilities, 10 in FY27)
rows.why: Five additional emerging-market facility expansions were announced in Q2 and 10 of 17 are due to go live in FY27.

rows.label: Headcount reduction, AI and automation cost programme
rows.why: Management cited headcount reduction, AI and automation as cost actions against integration and commodity headwinds, with 1,000+ automation projects targeted by next year and about 940 already in the pipeline.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book (USD 106 billion), US CV ramp and consumer electronics timing, but cautious on margins, Europe demand and copper working capital, and repeatedly declined margin or volume guidance; analysts pushed on pass-through status, Autoelectric's contribution to harne
